sources.title: Run LLMs locally on your Mac (Apple Silicon) · mlx-optiq
sources.snippet: Yes. mlx-optiq runs large language models natively on Apple Silicon, from M1 to M5, using Apple's MLX framework. Install it from PyPI with pip install mlx-optiq, then quantize, fine-tune, and serve models entirely on your Mac, fully offline.

sources.title: MLX models for Mac: 4-bit quants with size and RAM for each
sources.snippet: Pre-built quants · Hugging Face OptiQ quants, ready to load. Every model is a standard MLX checkpoint. Load it with mlx_lm.load (...), no special runtime and no PyTorch. OptiQ measures each layer's sensitivity and spends bits where they matter, so a mixed-precision quant keeps the accuracy a flat uniform quant gives up, at the same size.
